item.title: Essex at 7, Tuesday 17 November: Southend cabinet backs £800,000 plan to remove Three Shells Lagoon
item.description: The Seax morning briefing for Tuesday 17 November.
item.content:encoded:
Weather

Heavy rain, high 12°C, low 7°C, 60% chance of rain.

The stories that matter

Southend cabinet backs £800,000 plan to remove Three Shells Lagoon

Southend-on-Sea · Southend-on-Sea City Council's cabinet agreed on Monday night to clear the fenced-off lagoon beside Southend Pier and return the site to natural beach, a decade after it was built for nearly £2m.

Wet and windy start to Tuesday across Essex, with gusts close to 40mph

Essex · The heaviest rain is forecast in the early hours, before the wind peaks in the morning and brighter weather arrives on Wednesday.

Public inquiry into land for Chelmsford's £81m Army and Navy scheme opens next week

Chelmsford, Army and Navy roundabout · A government-appointed inspector will hear objections to the land deals and road changes Essex County Council needs to replace the Army and Navy roundabout in Chelmsford.

Home Office asks ministers, not Braintree council, to approve longer life for Wethersfield asylum centre

Wethersfield, Braintree · Braintree District Council's leader called the application for the former airfield near Wethersfield incredibly disappointing and said the council will take legal advice on any decision to extend it.

Police concerned for missing Clacton girl Hannah Steer, 15

Clacton · She has not been seen since about 9.30pm on Sunday, and Essex Police says officers need to find her to make sure she is ok.

Nearly 100 Colchester households stuck in B&Bs as emergency housing demand climbs

Colchester · Officers warn the city's homelessness budget will be heavily overspent this year as more families are placed in temporary homes.

Missing Grays pensioner Patrick Francisco, 83, has been found

Grays · Essex Police shared the good news on Monday night, a few hours after launching an urgent search for him.

Rosie the Jack Russell is dug out of a Maldon rabbit hole and learns absolutely nothing

Maldon · Firefighters cleared trees and dug with great care to free the terrier, who bolted for the next burrow the moment she was out.

From Council Watch

Auditors expect to give no opinion on three years of Basildon Council's accounts

Basildon Council · Basildon Borough Council's external auditors, EY, told councillors that the 2023/24, 2024/25 and 2025/26 accounts are all expected to receive disclaimed opinions, and listed borrowing, Sempra Homes…

Basildon Council borrowing stands at £727m as sale of its Dartford investment property is delayed

Basildon Council · Basildon Borough Council's leader told the Audit and Risk Committee he does not support adding to the council's long-term debt until the Dartford property is sold.

Travel

  • Colchester: Chitts Hill was closed on the evening of Mon 16 Nov after a three-vehicle crash; Essex Police asked drivers to avoid the area
  • Wickford: Runwell Road closed 8pm to 5am overnight on Sun 22 Nov for roadworks; First Essex X10 diverts via A130, A1245 and A127 and cannot serve Wickford
  • Thaxted: Dunmow Road closed for Essex Highways roadworks; long diversion in place
  • Basildon: Pipps Hill Road North and Hardings Elm Road closed between Oak Road and the A127 from Mon 9 Nov for about 26 days for gas mains work; diversion via A127, A132, A129 and A176

Results

  • Chelmsford Chieftains 6-3 Slough Jets (Challenge Cup)

On today

  • Mayor of Chelmsford's Cheese and Wine Evening, Chelmsford College, Princes Road, Chelmsford · £20

Every story links to the original reporting. More all day at theseax.com.

item.title: Essex at 7, Monday 16 November: Cheshunt man, 41, charged with arson over two Waltham Abbey shop fires
item.description: The Seax morning briefing for Monday 16 November.
item.content:encoded:
Weather

Sunny intervals, high 7°C, low 4°C, 40% chance of rain.

The stories that matter

Cheshunt man, 41, charged with arson over two Waltham Abbey shop fires

Waltham Abbey · Shorish Mahmoud, of Maple Lane, is due before Chelmsford magistrates on Wednesday 9 December.

New image in bid to name man found dead at Southend East 26 years ago

Southend-on-Sea, Southend East station · Locate International hopes a forensic artist's picture of 'Southend Station Man' as he may have looked around 1980 will be recognised by someone who knew him then.

Maldon Salt mixes German rock salt into its product, Observer finds

Goldhanger, Maldon · Lorries delivering bulk bags of mined salt were filmed at the firm's Goldhanger works. Regulators say the product is legally labelled.

Teenage boy wounded by air rifle in Chadwell St Mary street

Chadwell St Mary · Armed officers went to the scene in Chadwell St Mary, and Essex Police say they are following a number of targeted lines of enquiry.

Southend cabinet decides today whether to tear out Three Shells Lagoon and restore the beach

Southend-on-Sea · Removing the fenced-off seafront lagoon near Southend Pier would cost about £800,000, a decade after it was built for nearly £2m.

Missing Wickford man Simon Mahoney found safe, Essex Police say

Wickford · Officers had widened the search beyond Essex after he was caught on CCTV in Chelmsford shops on Friday.

Essex & Herts Air Ambulance calls on more women doctors and paramedics to join its helicopter crews

North Weald · Women are still a minority in helicopter emergency medicine across the UK, and the charity's flight doctor Kate Jackson has a simple message for anyone who doubts she belongs: apply.

Learn the 4Ts: Rayleigh mother shares her daughter's intensive care ordeal so parents spot type 1 diabetes sooner

Rayleigh · Mandy was told to prepare for the worst when Zara, then 13, reached Southend Hospital. Months of warning signs had gone unnoticed.

From Council Watch

Auditors expect to give no opinion on three years of Basildon Council's accounts

Basildon Council · Basildon Borough Council's external auditors, EY, told councillors that the 2023/24, 2024/25 and 2025/26 accounts are all expected to receive disclaimed opinions, and listed borrowing, Sempra Homes…

Basildon Council borrowing stands at £727m as sale of its Dartford investment property is delayed

Basildon Council · Basildon Borough Council's leader told the Audit and Risk Committee he does not support adding to the council's long-term debt until the Dartford property is sold.

Travel

  • Sun 15 Nov: some Liverpool Street platforms closed; Stansted Express every 30 minutes instead of 15, with extra Stratford to Stansted Airport trains via Tottenham Hale
  • Basildon: Pipps Hill Road North and Hardings Elm Road closed between Oak Road and the A127 from Mon 9 Nov for about 26 days for gas mains work; diversion via A127, A132, A129 and A176
  • 14 to 15 Nov: buses replace trains Sudbury to Marks Tey; Sunday also Ipswich to Colchester and Manningtree to Harwich
  • 21 to 22 Nov: no trains Braintree to Witham; Sunday also Colchester to Ingatestone

Results

  • Chelmsford Chieftains 6-3 Slough Jets (Challenge Cup)

Every story links to the original reporting. More all day at theseax.com.

item.title: Essex at 7, Sunday 15 November: Javelin great Fatima Whitbread made a Freewoman of Brentwood for her work with children in care
item.description: The Seax morning briefing for Sunday 15 November.
item.content:encoded:
Weather

Overcast with light rain at times, high 10°C, low 4°C, 70% chance of rain.

The stories that matter

Javelin great Fatima Whitbread made a Freewoman of Brentwood for her work with children in care

Brentwood · The former world champion, who grew up in children's homes, is the borough's newest honorary freewoman, just over a year after Thurrock gave her its own freedom.

Getting to an incident faster is no excuse, Essex chief warns after Braintree PC is sacked for speeding

Braintree · The Braintree-based constable broke the limit 75 times in marked police cars over two months and used blue lights without being trained as a response driver.

Community award winners to switch on Chelmsford's Christmas lights on Sunday

Chelmsford · A packed afternoon of music, markets and fairground rides builds to the 5pm switch-on, with fireworks to finish.

Thurrock's minor injuries unit leaves Orsett for a bigger home at Thurrock Hospital

Grays, Thurrock · The Thurrock walk-in unit now has its own plaster room, a wound care room with a shower and X-ray next door, and is open 10am to 7.30pm every day.

New CCTV pictures released in search for missing Wickford man Simon Mahoney

Wickford · Police think the 54-year-old may have taken a train through London to East Grinstead in West Sussex, and say they are extremely concerned for him.

Learn the 4Ts: Rayleigh mother shares her daughter's intensive care ordeal so parents spot type 1 diabetes sooner

Rayleigh · Mandy was told to prepare for the worst when Zara, then 13, reached Southend Hospital. Months of warning signs had gone unnoticed.

Dispersal order covers central Southend into the evening as pier lights return and fireworks light the seafront

Southend-on-Sea · Essex Police cited intelligence about possible trouble between groups of young supporters of Southend United and Aldershot Town.

NHS Essex puts £850,000 into braces to cut waits for young patients

Essex · Orthodontic practices across Essex will be paid to treat up to 500 extra children and young people.

Travel

  • Sun 15 Nov: some Liverpool Street platforms closed; Stansted Express every 30 minutes instead of 15, with extra Stratford to Stansted Airport trains via Tottenham Hale
  • Basildon: Pipps Hill Road North and Hardings Elm Road closed between Oak Road and the A127 from Mon 9 Nov for about 26 days for gas mains work; diversion via A127, A132, A129 and A176
  • 14 to 15 Nov: buses replace trains Sudbury to Marks Tey; Sunday also Ipswich to Colchester and Manningtree to Harwich
  • 21 to 22 Nov: no trains Braintree to Witham; Sunday also Colchester to Ingatestone

Results

  • Colchester United 2-0 Gillingham (League Two)
  • Brentwood Town 0-3 Ramsgate (Isthmian Premier)
  • Buckhurst Hill 2-1 AFC Sudbury (Isthmian North)
  • Concord Rangers 1-2 Bowers & Pitsea (Isthmian North)
  • Lewes 0-0 Stanway Rovers (Isthmian Premier)
  • Fakenham Town 1-1 Takeley (Isthmian North)
  • Felixstowe & Walton United 0-4 Tilbury (Isthmian North)
  • Grays Athletic 1-3 Gorleston (Isthmian North)

On today

  • Essex County Christmas Fair, Boreham House grounds, Boreham, Chelmsford · Adults £9 in advance, £12 on the day; under-3s free
  • Striking Comic Con Brentwood, Brentwood Centre, Pilgrims Hatch, Brentwood · Adults £10, children 5 to 12 £5, family £26, under-5s free
  • Chelmsford Christmas Lights Switch-On, Chelmsford city centre
  • Pavel Kolesnikov, Saffron Walden
  • The Ukulele Orchestra Of Great Britain, Westcliff-on-Sea

Every story links to the original reporting. More all day at theseax.com.

item.title: Essex at 7, Saturday 14 November: Inquest opens into death of Chelmsford boy, 2, who fell from Cyprus hotel window
item.description: The Seax morning briefing for Saturday 14 November.
item.content:encoded:
Weather

Sunny, high 8°C, low 2°C, 5% chance of rain.

The stories that matter

Inquest opens into death of Chelmsford boy, 2, who fell from Cyprus hotel window

Chelmsford · Jaxon Foster died from multiple severe injuries on the first day of a family holiday in July, Essex Coroner's Court has heard.

Anglia Ruskin University seeks voluntary redundancies to cut staff bill by 10%

Chelmsford · The university, which has campuses in Chelmsford plus Cambridge and Peterborough, spends about £150m a year on its workforce, the BBC reports.

Thurrock Council plans to save £995,000 as fewer families wait in emergency housing

Grays, Thurrock · Thurrock Council says the number of households it has placed in temporary accommodation is now falling by about 15 a month, after three years of steady rises.

Almost half of Stansted Airport passengers now arrive by train, bus or coach

Stansted · More than 13.5 million people used public transport to reach London Stansted Airport over the past 12 months, the Bishop's Stortford Independent reports.

Broomfield, Southend and Basildon hospital patients told to keep appointments as Microsoft email recovery continues

Chelmsford, Southend-on-Sea, Basildon · Microsoft says its email service is approaching normal levels after the global outage, but some messages are still arriving late.

Former PC who saw cyclist heading into traffic before fatal A130 crash would have been sacked, hearing rules

Chelmsford · A misconduct hearing chaired by Essex Police Chief Constable Rachel Nolan found Nicholas Davies did not stop, turn round or report the rider he had seen in Chelmsford.

Essex football and cricket clubs to lead year-long push on men's mental health

Essex · Essex County Council is funding the Colchester United, Southend United and West Ham United community foundations, with cricket partners, to reach men through sport across the county.

Maldon MP warns Hammonds Farm garden community could clog the A414 into town

Maldon, Heybridge · Sir John Whittingdale has written to the planning inspector examining Chelmsford's Local Plan, saying the 3,000-home scheme would leave Maldon and Heybridge with worse congestion and few other routes.

From Council Watch

Maldon council agrees to buy two plots at Langford to protect wildlife habitat from inappropriate use

Maldon District Council · Maldon District Council will try to buy two parcels of land at Langford, near Maldon, sold at auction in 2025, and can pay up to 10% above an independent valuation to secure the deal.

New rules for licensed pet and animal businesses across Basildon borough adopted until 2031

Basildon Council · Basildon Council has formally adopted an Animal Activity Licensing Policy and Animal Charter for 2026 to 2031, replacing its old Animal Welfare Charter after a public consultation.

Travel

  • Sun 15 Nov: some Liverpool Street platforms closed; Stansted Express every 30 minutes instead of 15, with extra Stratford to Stansted Airport trains via Tottenham Hale
  • Basildon: Pipps Hill Road North and Hardings Elm Road closed between Oak Road and the A127 from Mon 9 Nov for about 26 days for gas mains work; diversion via A127, A132, A129 and A176
  • 14 to 15 Nov: buses replace trains Sudbury to Marks Tey; Sunday also Ipswich to Colchester and Manningtree to Harwich
  • 21 to 22 Nov: no trains Braintree to Witham; Sunday also Colchester to Ingatestone

On today

  • Beer by the Pier: Southend Beer and Cider Festival, The Palace Hotel, Church Street, Southend-on-Sea · £5, free for CAMRA members
  • Essex County Christmas Fair, Boreham House grounds, Boreham, Chelmsford · Adults £9 in advance, £12 on the day; under-3s free
  • Southend Christmas Lights Switch On, High Street and seafront, Southend · Free
  • Tiptree Christmas Festival, Tiptree
  • Artisan Market at Festival Leisure Park, Festival Leisure Park, Basildon · Free entry, free parking

Every story links to the original reporting. More all day at theseax.com.

item.title: Essex at 7, Friday 13 November: No direct summer flight from Stansted to Florence once British Airways leaves the airport
item.description: The Seax morning briefing for Friday 13 November.
item.content:encoded:
Weather

Sunny, high 7°C, low -2°C, 5% chance of rain.

The stories that matter

No direct summer flight from Stansted to Florence once British Airways leaves the airport

Stansted · British Airways CityFlyer is pulling out of the Uttlesford airport after the 2026/27 ski season, but Ryanair will keep flying to Bergerac, Nice, Olbia and Palma.

Frost for Essex as Chelmsford is forecast to fall to -2C before Friday dawn

Essex · Clear skies are bringing a frost across Essex, with the Met Office forecasting a sunny but cold Friday 13 November before milder, wetter weather arrives at the weekend.

Police concerned for missing Harlow man, 30, last seen near Latton Common

Harlow · Essex Police are asking people in Harlow to look out for William Knight and the white Seat Ateca he was driving.

Agency nurse told Colchester care home colleague he would 'kill' his whole family, panel finds

Colchester · A Nursing and Midwifery Council panel found Rupesh Patel, 40, was drunk on a night shift at The Oaks care home in Colchester when he threatened a colleague, and he is set to be struck off.

Hanningfield among England's most depleted reservoirs as Essex hosepipe ban enters fourth month

Hanningfield · Hanningfield and Abberton, which supply much of mid and south Essex, held 37% of their capacity on 10 November, below average for the time of year, Essex & Suffolk Water says.

Six-vehicle M25 crash between the M11 and Waltham Abbey brings hour-long delays to morning rush

Waltham Abbey · Two of the four anticlockwise lanes near Waltham Abbey had reopened after the pile-up, with Essex Police saying nobody was reported hurt.

Suspected drug-drivers in Essex barred from driving for up to six weeks while police investigate

Essex · Essex Police says it is one of the first forces in the country to use bail conditions this way, as drug-driving arrests across the county keep rising.

Burnham-on-Crouch signs friendship pact with Carpathian town of Yaremche

Burnham-on-Crouch · Burnham-on-Crouch Town Council has become the first in Essex to twin with a Ukrainian community, linking the River Crouch town with Yaremche in the Ivano-Frankivsk region.

From Council Watch

Developer appeals over lack of decision on 910 green belt homes at Billericay's Foots Farm

Basildon Council · Basildon Borough Council's Planning Committee was asked to say how it would have decided the Great Burstead scheme, after an appeal was lodged because no decision had been made. Officers backed the…

Tendring councillors to vote on sending Local Plan for 1,069 homes a year to a government inspector

Tendring District Council · Tendring District Council's local plan committee meets on 17 November to decide whether to recommend submitting the plan, with Kirby Cross, Brightlingsea, Bradfield and Frinton sites drawing most…

Basildon councillors confirm refusal of 175 green belt homes at Little Burstead

Basildon Council · Basildon Borough Council's Planning Committee agreed the formal grounds for turning down homes west of Tye Common Road, near Billericay, going against officers' advice to approve.

Travel

  • Sun 15 Nov: some Liverpool Street platforms closed; Stansted Express every 30 minutes instead of 15, with extra Stratford to Stansted Airport trains via Tottenham Hale
  • Basildon: Pipps Hill Road North and Hardings Elm Road closed between Oak Road and the A127 from Mon 9 Nov for about 26 days for gas mains work; diversion via A127, A132, A129 and A176
  • 14 to 15 Nov: buses replace trains Sudbury to Marks Tey; Sunday also Ipswich to Colchester and Manningtree to Harwich
  • 21 to 22 Nov: no trains Braintree to Witham; Sunday also Colchester to Ingatestone

On today

  • Beer by the Pier: Southend Beer and Cider Festival, The Palace Hotel, Church Street, Southend-on-Sea · £5, free for CAMRA members
  • Essex County Christmas Fair, Boreham House grounds, Boreham, Chelmsford · Adults £9 in advance, £12 on the day; under-3s free
  • Chai Lates, Colchester Arts Centre, Colchester · £5
  • Stewart Lee vs The Man-Wulf, Chelmsford
  • Three Ravens Live: Friday 13th folklore, Colchester · £15

Every story links to the original reporting. More all day at theseax.com.

item.title: Essex at 7, Thursday 12 November: Two 18-year-olds and a boy of 17 arrested after man is stabbed in Basildon's East Walk
item.description: The Seax morning briefing for Thursday 12 November.
item.content:encoded:
Weather

Sunny, high 8°C, low 1°C, 10% chance of rain.

The stories that matter

Two 18-year-olds and a boy of 17 arrested after man is stabbed in Basildon's East Walk

Basildon · The man went into a nearby business for help on Tuesday evening and was taken to hospital; his injuries are not thought to be life-threatening.

Pedestrian suffers potentially serious leg injury at Harlow crossing as police seek white or silver car

Harlow · Essex Police say the car is reported to have gone through red lights at the Old House Croft crossing near Burnt Mill School in Harlow on Halloween evening and then left the scene.

Southend council says it cannot step in to reopen Leigh North Street school's shut swimming pool

Leigh-on-Sea · A report for Monday's cabinet says the pool's future is a matter for the school, despite a petition signed by more than 2,500 people.

Half-term getaway gives Stansted its busiest day ever with 109,881 passengers

Stansted · October brought 2.79 million travellers through the Uttlesford airport, up 4.2% on the same month last year.

Essex's first frost of the autumn expected as Chelmsford is forecast to drop to minus 1C on Friday night

Essex · Clear, dry weather across Essex brings sharp overnight falls in temperature before milder, wetter air returns at the weekend, the Met Office forecast shows.

Brentwood centre for rape and sexual assault survivors reopens after refit with new aftercare rooms

Brentwood · The Essex Sexual Assault Referral Centre, paid for by the county's police commissioner with Essex Police, stays in the county so survivors need not travel elsewhere.

Festoon lights back on Southend Pier for the first time in over 20 years, with switch-on set for Saturday

Southend-on-Sea · More than a mile of lights will run the length of the pier, launching an evening of festive events across the city on 14 November.

Developer seeks permission for 170 homes on Hutton green belt land

Hutton, Brentwood · A planning application has been lodged for new housing on green belt land at Hutton, near Brentwood, close to a country park.

From Council Watch

Developer appeals over lack of decision on 910 green belt homes at Billericay's Foots Farm

Basildon Council · Basildon Borough Council's Planning Committee was asked to say how it would have decided the Great Burstead scheme, after an appeal was lodged because no decision had been made. Officers backed the…

Tendring councillors to vote on sending Local Plan for 1,069 homes a year to a government inspector

Tendring District Council · Tendring District Council's local plan committee meets on 17 November to decide whether to recommend submitting the plan, with Kirby Cross, Brightlingsea, Bradfield and Frinton sites drawing most…

Basildon councillors confirm refusal of 175 green belt homes at Little Burstead

Basildon Council · Basildon Borough Council's Planning Committee agreed the formal grounds for turning down homes west of Tye Common Road, near Billericay, going against officers' advice to approve.

Travel

  • Basildon: Pipps Hill Road North and Hardings Elm Road closed between Oak Road and the A127 from Mon 9 Nov for about 26 days for gas mains work; diversion via A127, A132, A129 and A176
  • 14 to 15 Nov: buses replace trains Sudbury to Marks Tey; Sunday also Ipswich to Colchester and Manningtree to Harwich
  • 21 to 22 Nov: no trains Braintree to Witham; Sunday also Colchester to Ingatestone
  • 28 to 29 Nov: buses replace trains from Southend Victoria and Ingatestone towards Newbury Park, and Southminster to Wickford

Results

  • Salisbury 2-0 Braintree Town (National League South)
  • Colchester United 0-0 Ipswich Town U21 (EFL Trophy)

On today

  • Archive Explorers Club, Essex Record Office, Chelmsford · Free
  • Beer by the Pier: Southend Beer and Cider Festival, The Palace Hotel, Church Street, Southend-on-Sea · £5, free for CAMRA members
  • Simon Brodkin: Unleashed, Colchester
  • Stewart Lee vs The Man-Wulf, Chelmsford

Every story links to the original reporting. More all day at theseax.com.

item.title: Essex at 7, Wednesday 11 November: More than 23 years of jail terms over Epping Bell Hotel disorder after Loughton man, 34, is locked up
item.description: The Seax morning briefing for Wednesday 11 November.
item.content:encoded:
Weather

Light rain, high 10°C, low 4°C, 90% chance of rain.

The stories that matter

More than 23 years of jail terms over Epping Bell Hotel disorder after Loughton man, 34, is locked up

Epping, Loughton · Keith Silk was given two years and 11 months at Chelmsford Crown Court for violent disorder and criminal damage outside the hotel.

Man in his 80s dies after car hits two pedestrians in Mount Bures, near Colchester

Mount Bures, Colchester · A woman in her 70s is still being treated in hospital after Sunday's collision on Hall Road, and police are appealing for footage.

Basildon Council now expects a £3.8m overspend this year, with temporary housing for homeless families the biggest strain

Basildon · A half-year report warns reserves of £41.1m could be largely used up by 2029/30 if gaps keep being covered from savings, though it calls that a scenario rather than a forecast.

Parish councils object as Saturday deadline nears for comments on data centre at Little Canfield's old Crumps Farm landfill

Little Canfield, Dunmow · Little Canfield and Great Canfield parish councils have raised fears over contaminated land, water supply and the countryside as Essex County Council weighs the 10,240 sq m scheme near Dunmow.

National Highways asks Thurrock to hold off on 200-home Grey Goose Farm scheme in Grays until February as residents object

Grays · Persimmon wants outline permission for homes north of Long Lane, but the roads agency says more modelling is needed on the busy North Stifford junction first.

Plans that could see asylum seekers housed near Maldon raise concerns in a rural village

Maldon · New plans could see asylum seekers housed in a rural village near Maldon, prompting local concerns, the Daily Gazette reports.

Walk-in X-rays and new scans coming to St Margaret's diagnostic centre in Epping from mid-December

Epping · Blood tests move into the new community diagnostic centre at St Margaret's Hospital on 16 November, with X-ray, ultrasound and liver scans following on 14 December.

Hidden faces, street drinking and e-scooters on footpaths could all bring fines in Harlow under council plans open until 5 January

Harlow · Harlow Council wants residents' views on a package of Public Space Protection Orders, some town-wide and some for set places, with breaches punishable by fixed penalties or prosecution.

From Council Watch

Government direction pushes Southend's draft local plan towards a six-week public consultation

Southend-on-Sea City Council · The new plan would set the rules for where homes go and how the council handles applications for shared houses, affordable housing and hot food takeaways.

Auditors flag £1.7m pension difference in Southend's accounts but expect to finish on time

Southend-on-Sea City Council · KPMG told councillors its audit of the 2025/26 accounts is on track, with work still under way on the value of council homes.

Tendring households can now recycle glass at the kerbside after 70,000 extra boxes go out

Tendring District Council · The council's environment lead told cabinet the expanded collections began on 5 October, and arts grants to the district have risen six-fold.

Travel

  • Basildon: Pipps Hill Road North and Hardings Elm Road closed between Oak Road and the A127 from Mon 9 Nov for about 26 days for gas mains work; diversion via A127, A132, A129 and A176
  • c2c: trains due to call at Dagenham Dock, Rainham and Purfleet again from today, Wed 11 Nov, after Barking derailment repairs
  • 14 to 15 Nov: buses replace trains Sudbury to Marks Tey; Sunday also Ipswich to Colchester and Manningtree to Harwich
  • 21 to 22 Nov: no trains Braintree to Witham; Sunday also Colchester to Ingatestone

Results

  • Salisbury 2-0 Braintree Town (National League South)
  • Colchester United 0-0 Ipswich Town U21 (EFL Trophy)
  • Chelmsford City 2-2 Ebbsfleet United (National League South)

On today

  • Festival of Business: Proud Past, Bold Future, Braxted Park Estate, Great Braxted · Free visitor entry and parking (register first)
  • Port of Tilbury Maritime Remembrance Service, International Cruise Terminal, Tilbury · Free
  • Armistice Day service at Saffron Walden War Memorial, War Memorial, High Street, Saffron Walden · Free

Every story links to the original reporting. More all day at theseax.com.

item.title: Essex at 7, Tuesday 10 November: Russell Brand, who grew up in Grays, could challenge his 10-and-a-half-year rape sentence, solicitor tells the Standard
item.description: The Seax morning briefing for Tuesday 10 November.
item.content:encoded:
Weather

Cloudy, high 10°C, low 8°C, 40% chance of rain.

The stories that matter

Russell Brand, who grew up in Grays, could challenge his 10-and-a-half-year rape sentence, solicitor tells the Standard

Grays · A criminal defence solicitor not involved in the case told the Evening Standard an appeal against the sentence was the most likely next step, after the comedian was jailed at Southwark Crown Court on Monday.

Police still seeking witnesses to Sunday's early-hours crash that killed two people on Chelmsford's Copperfield Road

Chelmsford · Essex Police wants doorbell, dashcam and eyewitness accounts after a driver and passenger died when their Ford Fiesta struck a property wall near Havisham Way.

Southend's fenced-off Three Shells Lagoon should be removed and the beach restored, council report says

Southend-on-Sea · Southend-on-Sea City Council says taking out the failed lagoon is its preferred long-term option, and the proposal goes to Cabinet on 16 November.

Braintree and County Hall leaders vow to resist Home Office bid to keep Wethersfield asylum site open after April 2027

Wethersfield, Braintree · The government has applied to extend its use of the former airbase near Braintree, where asylum seekers have been housed since July 2023, and both councils say they will look at ways to oppose it.

Harlow college shut over building safety fears wins approval for a permanent new school

Harlow · Sir Frederick Gibberd College pupils have been taught in temporary classrooms for two years after the modular main building was closed.

Maldon council says national rules leave little room to refuse new homes in Tollesbury, Great Totham and Latchingdon

Maldon, Tollesbury, Great Totham, Latchingdon · The district's leader says unpopular village schemes cannot be turned down without sound planning evidence, as a new national scheme also takes many decisions away from committee.

Multi-agency raids on more than 100 Essex premises seize £10,360 in cash and illicit cigarettes

Essex · Operation Machinize, coordinated by the National Crime Agency and carried out locally by Essex Police with partner agencies, targeted organised crime linked to businesses across the county.

Southend council still heading for a £12m overspend as one child's care placement tops £1m a year

Southend-on-Sea · The latest six-month forecast shows the gap narrowing by about £1.3m, but children's social care costs have climbed by around £1.5m since the summer.

From Council Watch

Government direction pushes Southend's draft local plan towards a six-week public consultation

Southend-on-Sea City Council · The new plan would set the rules for where homes go and how the council handles applications for shared houses, affordable housing and hot food takeaways.

Southend aims to bring council home repairs up to industry norms by Christmas after regulator judgement

Southend-on-Sea City Council · Electrical safety checks on council homes are now close to complete, but councillors heard that repairs remain the weak spot in Southend's response to the social housing regulator.

Three in four Thurrock children entering care now get their first health check on time, up from 36%

Thurrock Council · Councillors scrutinising children's services heard that initial health assessments within the 20-day legal deadline have more than doubled.
